findings.title: R2's fix overclaims in the other direction: 'nothing is asking for' concurrent pods is contradicted by M4's own acceptance criterion 2, which asks for N CONCURRENT contenders over >=100 seeds and which no backlog row owns
findings.failure_scenario: M4/SPEC.md:392-394 reads: 'Exactly one winner under lease contention: with N concurrent contenders racing an unheld or expired lease, exactly one acquires it and every other receives an empty Optional and backs off. Asserted over >=100 seeds.' Nothing in the tree meets it: LeaseManagerConcurrencyTest is two threads, one case, no seeds, and asserts one winner on one instance rather than N contenders over >=100 seeds; the driver never has two contenders in one round at all (when leaderless it draws exactly ONE pod and calls tryStart once), so its 'many logical pods' does not touch criterion 2 either; and grepping backlog.md for the criterion finds no owning row. FAILURE: this file is where a reader auditing M4's completion condition now lands -- that is the whole reason R2 was raised -- and it tells them the demand does not exist. M4 is then declared complete with criterion 2 neither met nor recorded, which is the same harm R2 named, arriving through an absence-of-demand claim instead of a wrong pointer. The claim is also of the shape this repository deletes on sight (crossEpochOffsetsChecked, M4.19): 'nothing is asking for it' cannot go false, because no gate can range over what nothing asks for. SECONDARY, same clause and same remedy: the sentence 'here is where that race IS covered' has 'two writers racing one slot IN REAL TIME' as its antecedent, and the two tests it then names do not race in real time -- CommitLogSealWriteTest hand-plants the fenced leader's delta and StealFirstPutStore pre-writes the winning bytes inside putIfAbsent, both single-threaded. What those tests cover is the LOST-SLOT BRANCH, deterministically, which is the substantive thing; the words claim more. REMEDY (a backlog row, not a code change -- review.md rule 11): drop 'which nothing is asking for' and say instead that M4 criterion 2's >=100-seed contention assertion is unowned, and that the chain-slot loss is covered deterministically rather than by concurrency.

findings.title: An AMBIGUOUS fault on a zombie's delta is booked as 'the zombie discovered it is fenced', so zombieWrites -- the number the test says records 'fenced writes that LANDED' and M4.16 is to drive to zero -- can undercount by construction
findings.failure_scenario: FaultInjectingStore.putIfAbsent's ambiguous arm writes through to the delegate and THEN throws (verified at FaultInjectingStore.java:239-248, and M4.12's row states it as the modelled gap). The driver's zombie branch catches that IOException, comments 'correct: the zombie discovered it is fenced', removes the zombie from the list and does NOT increment zombieWrites -- yet the bytes are in the chain, and the writer was not fenced, it got an ambiguous response. Two consequences: the fenced writer stops being simulated (less of the contention this branch exists to create), and zombieWrites understates landed fenced writes. That matters because CommitProtocolSimulationTest.java:114 describes the number as 'fenced writes that LANDED across the range' and M4.16 is to drive it to zero -- a metric that can miss a landing is a weaker signal of that fix than it reads as. MEASURED, and this is why it is only minor: over seeds 0..29 at ROUGH I counted the deltas actually in the store whose segmentKey starts 'seg/zombie-' and got 7, exactly equal to the reported zombieWrites=7, so there is no live discrepancy today. But the agreement is luck, not structure -- there are 15 zombie attempts in that range at p(ambiguousPut)=0.05, so ~0.75 undercounts are expected per sweep, and the count moves the moment the fault rates or the seed range do. Nothing asserts zombieWrites (it is `isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(0)`), so no test changes colour either way; the correction belongs with whoever reads the number, i.e. M4.16.
